title: Constrained hosted API PRD: dry-run canary + minimal behavioral surface
creator: Maya Chen
summary: PRD for launching a constrained, minimal-behavior variant of the hosted inference API (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) behind a dry-run canary. Focus: strict acceptance criteria, synthetic dry-run traffic, explicit behavior gating and rollback mechanics to validate telemetry, costs, and quality before broad enablement.
background: There is ongoing work to unify generation, embedding, and reranking surfaces across hosted and dedicated modes. Past launches revealed subtle behavioral drift across model variants and unexpected cost spikes under realistic traffic shapes. This PRD defines a conservative, observable-first rollout path: a minimal feature surface that can be exercised with synthetic users and limited customer pilots to validate behavior-contracts, SLOs, and cost economics prior to opening to general usage.
goals: Validate behavioral contracts for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank endpoints using a standardized prompt set and automated comparators
Prove telemetry and alerting (per-route latency, p50/p90/p99, per-token cost, error classes) under representative dry-run traffic
Surface performance and cost regressions early via canary thresholds and automatic rollback triggers
Establish a repeatable launch checklist and acceptance harness for future hosted endpoint rollouts
success_metrics: Per-route p95 latency < 220ms for short chats (<=128 tokens) during dry-run traffic
Error rate <= 0.5% (5xx + model-compat errors) during dry-run traffic
Per-token cost variance within +/-10% of baseline during synthetic traffic
Quality regression score: automated prompt-set pass rate >= 95% (see acceptance_criteria)
Monitoring coverage: telemetry events emitted for 100% of requests in dry-run lanes
scope_included: A minimal hosted API surface with toggled features: generation (completions), chat (single-turn + streaming), embeddings (single vector), and rerank (rank-by-score)
Dry-run canary lane: traffic routed to canary for telemetry capture but not billed to end customers until pilot opt-in
Prompt-set based acceptance harness: canonical test prompts for each surface (customer-like, adversarial, edge cases)
Telemetry dashboard and alerting runbook for the canary lane
Automated rollback policy based on telemetry thresholds
scope_excluded: Full multi-turn chat state management and long-sequence performance tuning beyond 1024 tokens
Regional multi-zone traffic routing; dry-run will run in a single region only
Dedicated capacity and private/VPC deployment paths (not in scope for this PRD)
Advanced function/tool calling or multimodal inputs
acceptance_criteria: Functional correctness: all endpoints return responses conforming to the agreed surface contract (JSON schema and status codes) for 100% of canonical prompt-set requests
Quality threshold: automated comparator (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity classifier) flags <=5% regressions vs baseline for generation and chat prompts
Rerank parity: top-3 ordering stability >= 95% against baseline reranker for the canonical dataset
Embedding drift: mean cosine similarity to baseline embeddings >= 0.92 across benchmark corpus
Observability: every request emitted events: request.start, request.end, model.variant, tokens.consumed, route.id
Alerting: green->amber->red thresholds defined and tested; alert runbook steps validated by an on-call drill
Cost control: synthetic run budget capped; autoscaling shall not exceed the cost cap during dry-run
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dry-run: route 2% synthetic traffic from test harness to canary lane for 48h. 2) Expanded dry-run: increase to 10% synthetic traffic and run for 7 days, run automated acceptance harness hourly. 3) Customer pilot: invite 2–3 trusted customers to opt in to the dry-run lane (metered but not billed for experimentation) and run for 2 weeks. 4) Decision gate: signoff meeting with PM, Eng, Design, Security; if acceptance criteria met, schedule broader gradual enablement. Each step requires a go/no-go checklist and the automated rollback policy must be exercised in a staged failover test.
launch_checklist: PRD reviewed and approved by Eng, Design, Security, and Observability leads
Acceptance harness with canonical prompt set implemented and stored in test artifacts
Canary deployment automated (IaC) with toggle and traffic-slicing controls
Dashboards created: per-route latency/cost/throughput and quality regression graphs
Alerts configured: latency p95, error rate, cost cap breach, quality regression spike
Runbook drafted with rollback steps and on-call responsibilities
Synthetic traffic generator validated and budgeted (cost cap set)
Customer pilot invitations and NDA/opt-in mechanics ready
Security review completed and KMS/access scoped for dry-run telemetry
Post-mortem template ready for dry-run incidents
monitoring_alerts: Latency-p95 > 300ms for 5m -> alert on-call and auto-scale prevented; trigger amber status
Error-rate > 0.5% for 10m -> paging to SRE with rollback checklist
Quality-regression delta > 5% (hourly) -> notify ML/Research and pause expansion
Canary-cost burn rate exceeds budget by 15% in 1h -> automatic rollback to previous model variant
dependencies: Runtime team: canary deployment orchestration and kernel-selection pinning
Observability: dashboard panels, event schema, and retention configured
Research/Model Ops: baseline model variants and comparator tools for quality metrics
Billing: dry-run meter but do-not-bill configuration and cost-accounting
Legal: pilot opt-in terms and data-processing addendum for customer pilots
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regression escapes detection because synthetic prompt-set is incomplete -> Mitigation: add adversarial prompts and a small live-parity sample from anonymized customer logs
Risk: Cost spikes during autoscale -> Mitigation: hard cost cap with enforced autoscale ceiling in canary lane
Risk: Observability gaps (missing event emission) -> Mitigation: pre-launch smoke tests that validate event emission for 100% of requests
Risk: Customer confusion when exposed to dry-run behavior -> Mitigation: explicit labeling in pilot docs and separate telemetry namespace
open_questions: Q1: Should the dry-run lane be billable for customers in the pilot? (legal/billing input required)
Q2: What is the canonical baseline model checkpoint for each surface (gen/embed/rerank)?
Q3: Is streaming behavior parity required for the initial pilot or can streaming be toggled off?
Q4: Which regions are acceptable for customer pilot data residency constraints?
notes: This PRD emphasizes a conservative, telemetry-first path to reduce blast radius and learn quickly. The dry-run concept allows us to validate non-functional signals (cost, telemetry, regression detection) before exposing customers to potential behavior drift. Keep the initial surface intentionally small to minimize integration testing burden.
